results.title: An integrated human forebrain organoid reveals microglia-mediated CD8<sup>+</sup> T cell recruitment and neuroimmune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease pathology.
results.authorString: Feng Y, Yu F, Tang J, Zheng H, Wang Z, Ma S.
results.abstractText: Genetic evidence implicates immune dysfunction in Alzheimer's disease (AD), yet the neuroimmune mechanisms operating in human tissue remain poorly defined. Here, we establish a modular human forebrain organoid platform that systematically integrates human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived microglia and CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells to reconstitute multicellular AD pathology. This system enables functional interrogation of both innate and adaptive immune components in a human-relevant context. Using this platform, we demonstrate that microglia mediate amyloid-β clearance and neuronal maturation but also drive inflammatory activation and recruit CD8<sup>+</sup> T cells through CCL4/5 signaling via CCR1/5 and CXCR3, establishing a neuroinflammatory feedback loop. Pharmacological targeting of CCR5 or CXCR3 blocks T cell recruitment and modulates autophagy in a microglia-dependent manner. This modular organoid platform provides a versatile tool for dissecting neuron-immune interactions and enables cell-type-specific therapeutic screening in human neuroinflammatory disease models.

results.title: Toward Sensory Homeostasis in Autism: Comparative Evaluation of a Recurrent Signal-to-Memory Hierarchy
results.authorString: Gargus JJ.
results.abstractText:
Background:

/Objectives: The signal-to-memory (S2M) hierarchy links Ca²⁺-signal construction and decoding to transcriptional and chromatin changes that may modify subsequent neuronal responsiveness and support sensory homeostasis: adaptation to familiar input while preserving sensitivity to meaningful change. We assessed evidence for its involvement in autism spectrum disorder (ASD) pathogenesis and implications for therapeutic target validation.

Methods:

The prespecified S2M-44 core was compared with 11 monogenic ASD mouse models, an ASD protein-association network, and 106 schizophrenia-prioritized genes. Exact overlap, molecular association, and functional correspondence were distinguished; broader ASD-gene context and four extension candidates were evaluated separately.

Results:

Four mouse-model genes matched the core, all transcriptional or chromatin regulators. The protein network represented 27 core proteins, including both IP₃ receptors, ITPR1 and ITPR3, recovered as interactors. Separately reported KDM6B and SETD5 studies demonstrated rescue of downstream neuronal defects, with selected behavioral rescue in the SETD5 model. The schizophrenia set shared one core gene and implicated related signaling operations.

Conclusions:

These findings strengthen the case for pathogenic involvement of connected S2M operations and prioritize IP₃R-mediated Ca²⁺ release for molecular target validation. Demonstrating target-dependent restoration of signaling and adaptive responsiveness across genetically distinct models would establish a mechanistic foundation for drug discovery.

results.title: The Current Status and Evaluation of Artificial Intelligence in Bladder Cancer: Clinical Applications and Research.
results.authorString: Yin Z, Ho JWK.
results.abstractText: Bladder cancer ranks as the 10th most common malignancy worldwide. Advances in technology are continuously reshaping its diagnosis, treatment selection, and prognosis assessment. In recent years, artificial intelligence (AI) has demonstrated marked potential in transforming bladder cancer care. By integrating and analyzing multi-source data, AI enhances the precision and efficiency of disease management. This review comprehensively examines the current applications of AI across various domains, including radiographic imaging analysis, pathological diagnosis, cystoscopic image processing, molecular subtyping, drug development, organoid research, prognostic modeling, and medical device innovation. It highlights the advantages of AI over conventional methods, outlines model development strategies, and summarizes commonly employed algorithms. Furthermore, we discuss the key challenges in translating AI tools into real-world clinical practice. This narrative review aims to inform the future development of AI-driven digital health systems, ultimately contributing to the realization of precision medicine and personalized management for bladder cancer patients.

results.title: Targeting ubiquitin-dependent mitochondrial autophagy and apoptosis in sarcopenia: the therapeutic potential of phytochemicals.
results.authorString: Zeng Y, Wang P.
results.abstractText: Sarcopenia is a progressive degenerative disease of skeletal muscle closely associated with aging, disuse, and chronic diseases, affecting approximately 10-16% of the global older adult population. Its core pathological basis lies in the disruption of skeletal muscle cell proteostasis and mitochondrial dysfunction. At the molecular level, excessive degradation of structural proteins mediated by the ubiquitin-proteasome system forms an intertwined vicious cycle with the inability of ubiquitin-dependent mitophagy to clear damaged organelles, ultimately triggering irreversible cell death programmes within an oxidative stress and inflammatory microenvironment. Due to the high complexity and molecular crosstalk within this cell fate-determining network, traditional single-target interventions often yield limited therapeutic efficacy. In recent years, phytochemicals (such as polyphenols, flavonoids, alkaloids, and coumarins) have demonstrated significant therapeutic potential in the field of sarcopenia due to their unique multi-target, multi-pathway synergistic regulatory advantages. This article reviews the dual-faceted regulatory mechanisms of ubiquitination in skeletal muscle mitochondrial quality control, protein hydrolysis, and apoptosis escape and provides an analysis of how phytochemicals achieve autophagy-promoting, anti-apoptotic, and anti-degradative skeletal muscle protection. However, oral bioavailability is often below 1%, microbiota-dependent metabolism, and the absence of phase III clinical trials have hindered the translational application of phytochemicals. This paper explores the use of nano-delivery systems to overcome the bioavailability bottleneck of phytochemicals, as well as translational application strategies based on the gut-muscle axis to reshape the in vivo metabolism of natural products. This review aims to provide a solid theoretical foundation for the development of novel phytochemical-derived drugs targeting ubiquitination and apoptosis networks and to chart a course for reversing skeletal muscle ageing and enhancing human healthspan.

results.title: Epitope-diverse autoantibodies induce neutrophil-epithelial niches driving kidney injury in ANCA-associated glomerulonephritis.
results.authorString: Nishide M, Matsushita H, Mizuno Y, Nishimura K, Lelliott PM, Kawada S, Fujii T, Kamikawaji S, Nonaka T, Motooka D, Metsugi S, Shimagami H, Miyamoto AT, Kato Y, Tsujimoto K, Edahiro R, Shirai Y, Yamamoto Y, Naito Y, Konaka H, Izumi M, Naito M, Nakanishi Y, Namba-Hamano T, Inoue K, Takahashi A, Mizui M, Nakazawa S, Kakuta Y, Funakoshi K, Terada M, Irie M, Torizawa T, Omiya R, Smith NI, Isaka Y, Nonomura N, Okada Y, Hattori K, Narazaki M, Kumanogoh A.
results.abstractText: Autoantibody-mediated inflammation drives tissue injury in autoimmune diseases, yet how pathogenic antibodies evoke local immune activation remains poorly understood. Here, we show that spatially organized neutrophil-epithelial niches contribute to kidney injury in myeloperoxidase (MPO)-antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibody-associated glomerulonephritis. Single-cell-resolved spatial transcriptomics of treatment-naïve patient kidney biopsies identified early-phase inflammatory niches enriched with HAVCR1+ injured proximal tubular epithelial cells, neutrophils, lymphocytes, and TREM2+ macrophages. Injured epithelial cells expressed chemokines including CXCL6 and CXCL16, defining a microenvironment associated with local immune cell accumulation. Neutrophils within these niches were characterized by transcriptional programs enriched for type II interferon and Fcγ receptor (FcγR)-related signaling. Mechanistically, combinations of monoclonal anti-MPO antibodies recognizing distinct epitopes enhanced neutrophil activation and induced pauci-immune crescentic glomerulonephritis in mice, recapitulating key aspects of epithelial injury observed in human kidneys. One-armed anti-MPO antibodies engineered to minimize FcγR engagement ameliorated kidney injury in mice. Together, these findings identify pathogenic neutrophil-epithelial niche formation as a driver of autoimmune kidney injury.

results.title: Tubocapsenolide A Overcomes Oxaliplatin Resistance in Colorectal Cancer by Targeting PLK1 to Impair CEP55-ESCRT-Associated Vesicular Damage Clearance.
results.authorString: Yang Y, Liang J, Wang L, Zhang H, Zhang Z, Liu Y, Zhu R, Xu W, Xu S, Sun D, Xiang K, Wang Y, Fan Z, Wang Z, Li H, Chen L.
results.abstractText: Oxaliplatin (L-OHP) is a first-line chemotherapeutic agent for advanced colorectal cancer (CRC) and postoperative adjuvant therapy. However, acquired L-OHP resistance remains a clinical obstacle. Here, we identify Tubocapsenolide A (TA), a natural withanolide isolated from Tubocapsicum anomalum, as a promising antitumor agent that suppresses CRC growth and sensitizes L-OHP-resistant CRC to L-OHP. Using a PROTAC-based target deconvolution strategy, we identify PLK1 as a direct molecular target of TA. PLK1 is elevated in L-OHP-resistant CRC and is associated with reduced patient sensitivity to L-OHP. Mechanistically, elevated PLK1 promotes CEP55 Ser436 phosphorylation and facilitates ESCRT recruitment to nuclear and mitochondrial budding sites. This process facilitates the clearance of L-OHP-induced damaged components through nuclear budding and TOM20<sup>-</sup>/PDH<sup>+</sup> mitochondrial-derived vesicles, thereby contributing to organelle homeostasis and cell survival. By inhibiting PLK1, TA interferes with this vesicle-associated damage clearance process, leading to intracellular accumulation of damaged components. This damage accumulation is accompanied by nucleolar stress and mitochondrial dysfunction, ultimately contributing to cell death. Collectively, our findings identify a previously unappreciated role of the PLK1-CEP55-ESCRT axis in vesicle-associated damage clearance during L-OHP resistance and support this axis as a potential therapeutic target. TA represents a promising lead compound for overcoming L-OHP resistance in CRC.

results.title: A Micropeptide Component of the OGDH Complex Modulates ATP Production in the TCA Cycle.
results.authorString: Yin X, Qi W, Lin L, Zheng H, Zhao G, Chen Q, Shao G, Wu Y, Hu J, Xu H.
results.abstractText: Since its elucidation, the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle has been regarded as a fully defined enzymatic pathway. Here, we report the discovery of a previously unrecognized micropeptide component of this central metabolic system. Through analyzing ribosome profiling data from the mouse sORFs.org database, we discovered APPM (ATP production-promoting micropeptide), a 29-amino acid peptide encoded by a non-canonical small open reading frame within the mouse Ctsb gene. APPM localizes to the mitochondrial matrix and inner membrane, where it directly binds to the E1 subunit (OGDH) of the α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex (OGDHc). This interaction modulates OGDHc enzymatic activity, thereby regulating NADH and ATP production. We identified tyrosine-13 as the critical residue mediating the APPM-OGDH interaction and functional activation. Exogenous APPM administration increased ATP levels in vivo and, in a mouse model of heart failure, restored cardiac function, outperforming the reference drug trimetazidine. Collectively, our findings identify APPM as the first micropeptide regulator of the OGDH complex, expanding the known repertoire of the TCA cycle and presenting a potential therapeutic strategy for diseases characterized by bioenergetic insufficiency.

results.title: Long non-coding RNA LINC00885 contributes to liver steatosis through modulation of DHRS2-associated lipid metabolic programs.
results.authorString: Tsai KY, Wei PL, Su KY, Lee CC, Batzorig U, Huang CY, Chang YJ.
results.abstractText:
Background and aims

Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is a prevalent and rising liver disease. Its inflammatory subtype, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), can progress to fibrosis, cirrhosis, and hepatocellular carcinoma. The role of long intergenic non-protein coding RNA 885 (LINC00885) in MASLD remains unknown. This study aims to clarify its function in steatotic liver disease.

Methods

Public liver transcriptomic datasets, RNA sequencing of LINC00885-knockdown Hep G2 cells, and microarray profiling under lipotoxic conditions were integrated to identify candidate downstream components. Gain- and loss-of-function models, Oil Red O staining, RT-qPCR, an actinomycin D chase assay, functional rescue, and JC-1 analysis were used to evaluate the LINC00885-DHRS2 axis. Circulating exosomal RNA and exploratory ROC analyses were assessed in a pilot cohort.

Results

LINC00885 was upregulated in MASH liver tissue and induced by FFA treatment in hepatocytes. LINC00885 promoted lipid accumulation and shifted lipid metabolic gene expression toward lipogenesis. Integrated transcriptomic analyses identified DHRS2 as a convergent downstream candidate. LINC00885 knockdown increased DHRS2 expression and was associated with slower DHRS2 mRNA decay. DHRS2 exerted an anti-steatotic phenotype, and DHRS2 depletion reversed the reduction in lipid accumulation caused by LINC00885 knockdown. DHRS2 perturbation was also accompanied by changes in mitochondrial membrane potential. In a pilot serum cohort, exosomal LINC00885 and DHRS2 showed opposite expression patterns and preliminary discriminative potential.

Conclusions

The findings support a functional LINC00885-DHRS2 axis associated with hepatocellular lipid accumulation, lipid metabolic gene expression, and mitochondrial membrane potential. The circulating exosomal observations are exploratory and require validation in larger, clinically characterized cohorts.
